newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean defector to be flown to South by Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean defector to be flown to South by Tuesday.

text.p: A high-level North Korean defector taking refuge in the Philippines will arrive in South Korea by Tuesday, a senior Seoul foreign ministry official said.
"Mr Hwang Jang-yop will be flown to our country between April 20-22," the official told Reuters on Thursday, asking not to be identified.
Hwang, the most senior Pyongyang official ever to flee the communist country, has been sheltering at a hideout in the Philippines since March 18.

Hwang, chief architect of North Korea's ideology of "juche", a creed of self-reliance, went to South Korea's consulate in Beijing on February 12 and had to wait for more than a month before he was spirited out to the Philippines.

Diplomats have said China, which fought alongside North Korea in the 1950-53 Korean War, tried to save face for its ally by demanding that Hwang stay in the Philippines for about one month as part of its deal with Seoul to let Hwang leave.

Hwang slipped out of Beijing in secrecy last month and Philippine authorities have since kept him under wraps, mainly for security reasons. But Seoul indicated Hwang would end his odyssey in the glare of publicity.
South Korean information officials have told reporters they were arranging facilities for the media, including foreign journalists, to cover Hwang's arrival.
Security officials said Hwang, ranked 24th in Pyongyang's hierarchy, planned to issue a statement on arrival in South Korea. They said a plan had been finalised for bringing him to Seoul safely.
Seoul officials said Hwang was expected to leave the Philippines after the end of crucial talks in New York among senior diplomats from the two Koreas and the United States.
The diplomats met on Wednesday to hear Pyongyang's answer to an offer for peace talks aimed at securing a peace treaty to replace the truce that ended the Korean War.

The discussion was adjourned for two days. Participants refused to go into detail about why Wednesday's crucial meeting left the matter of North Korea's participation in landmark four-nation talks unresolved, but said they hoped to settle the issue on Friday.
The four-nation talks, also involving China, were proposed jointly by U.S. President Bill Clinton and his South Korean counterpart Kim Young-sam a year ago.
